CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Evelyn is a 56-year-old female with a past medical history significant for coronary artery disease with prior stenting, prior carpal tunnel release, and herniated disc presenting for her annual exam. The patient reports that her herniated disc has been doing well since a steroid injection several months ago with no back pain and no limitations in movement. Her carpal tunnel symptoms have resolved following prior release, she is back to work with full range of motion, and denies numbness and tingling in her hands. Regarding her coronary artery disease, over the last month she has been experiencing chest pain. She describes the pain as a burning sensation located in the middle of her chest. The pain occurs with walking and is relieved with rest. She denies chest pain at rest. She experiences the chest pain approximately three times per week. She denies associated shortness of breath, nausea, and vomiting.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for chest pain as described above and nasal congestion from allergies related to pollen. Negative for lower extremity edema, muscle aches, fever, and chills.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Coronary artery disease with prior stenting
Prior carpal tunnel release
Herniated disc

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Seasonal allergies (pollen).

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is back to work.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure well controlled, oxygenation normal.
Cardiovascular: Slight 3 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur.
Pulmonary: Lungs clear, no carotid bruits appreciated.
Extremities: No lower extremity edema. Healed surgical scars on right wrist.

RESULTS
Echocardiogram from last year: Left ventricular ejection fraction 45%, mild mitral regurgitation.
ECG: Stable, consistent with prior coronary artery disease, no new changes.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Carpal tunnel release: Patient doing well with no recurrent symptoms. No further intervention needed at this time. Patient instructed to report if symptoms recur.

2. Herniated disc: Patient doing well with no recurrent symptoms. No further steroid injection or physical therapy indicated at this time. Patient instructed to report if symptoms recur.

3. Coronary artery disease with recurrent chest pain: Continue aspirin and toprol. Stress test ordered to evaluate for additional coronary blockages. Lipid panel ordered. Starting crestor 20 mg once daily.
